task.description: REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2d) on REQ-164's decision artefact -- decision-record consistency and scope, no code. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already PASSed. Your job: confirm this artefact does not silently reopen or contradict decision 0014's premises, confirm the artefact's placement decision (lib/letflow/design/ vs. a new docs/migration/decisions/ record) is consistent with the REQ-163 precedent it claims to mirror, confirm no scope creep, and give a final sanity check on the REQ-175 cancellation consequence since a wrongly-triggered cancellation of a real requirement is a consequential, hard-to-reverse-cheaply action for the next DOC-UPDATER step to take.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm the artefact does not silently reopen or contradict decision 0014's settled premises.
Confirm the REQ-163 placement precedent the artefact cites is accurately characterized (re-read lib/letflow/design/req163-wasm-abi-choice.md's own placement rationale).

Confirm no scope creep: git diff --stat main...feature/WF02-REQ164-20260828 touches only this run's own handoffs/, docs/status/, handoffs/registry.json bookkeeping, and lib/letflow/design/req164-wasm-compilation-hosting.md.

Give a final sanity check specifically on the REQ-175 cancellation trigger: is the NO decision genuinely well-supported enough that cancelling a real, already-drafted requirement is the correct action, or does anything in REQ-175's own text suggest cancellation might be premature (e.g. a caller that already exists, a stakeholder commitment)? This is the one place in this run where a wrong call has real downstream cost.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

findings: No silent contradiction of decision 0014: the artefact answers exactly the open question 0014 itself deferred (OQ-3), does not touch 0014's Decision section (bind wasmex behind a process boundary), does not reopen the Lua half, and correctly treats S6's three named operational inputs (artifact storage, retention, job execution) as assumed-not-available rather than silently assuming them solved -- consistent with 0014's own framing that OQ-3 'needs S6's operational input.'

REQ-175 cancellation sanity check (most important item): read REQ-175's full entry in docs/requirements.yaml (lines 8880-8949). REQ-175 is explicitly self-conditional -- its own description states 'CONDITIONAL REQUIREMENT. This requirement exists only if REQ-164 decided YES... If REQ-164 decided NO, REQ-164's own acceptance criteria require this requirement to be CANCELLED with a status-history event recording why -- not left pending,' and acceptance criterion #1 restates the same instruction verbatim. There is no existing caller, no stakeholder commitment, and no ambiguity in the conditional framing -- REQ-175 was drafted anticipating precisely this NO outcome and wrote its own cancellation instruction in advance. REQ-164's artefact quotes this correctly and does not overreach: it recommends cancellation (DOC-UPDATER's job at Step 6) rather than performing it, and correctly leaves REQ-165/166/167/171/172 untouched since those operate on a .wasm artifact regardless of its origin. No sign cancellation is premature. depends_on for REQ-175 is [REQ-164, REQ-166], both fine to cancel against since REQ-166 is unaffected by this decision and REQ-164 (this run) is what triggers the cancellation.

Evidence chain (R-Co stubs, zero .wasm files, no Zig toolchain, build-farm security surface with no offsetting caller) is grounded in 0014's own already-verified quotes, not re-derived or embellished -- appropriate given the R-Co path's unreachability from this sandbox, consistent with REQ-163's precedent for the same limitation.

No decision-record disagreement to flag -- the artefact operates as designed: decision-only, no lib/ or mix.exs change, correctly routes the actual docs/requirements.yaml edit to DOC-UPDATER at Step 6.
